panels.title: How to read this dashboard

options.content:
**Story:** top → bottom goes from *is it alive?* to *how fast / how much?* to *which hardware resource is paying for it?* and finally *who is using it?*. Row 5 overlays application load on system metrics so a bulk-ZIP upload can be traced straight to its CPU / RAM footprint.  
**Colours:** Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe palette; series also differ by line dash, so print/PDF stays readable. Blue = healthy, orange = warning, vermillion = critical. Refresh: 5 s.

panels.title: 1 · Health at a glance
App status — Prometheus scrape of the Streamlit app
panels.description: UP when Prometheus can scrape the app's /metrics endpoint; DOWN otherwise.

panels.title: node_exporter — system-metrics scrape
panels.description: UP when node_exporter (CPU/RAM/disk metrics) is reachable.

panels.title: Alerts firing — count of active Prometheus alerts
panels.description: Number of alerts currently in the firing state (see alert_rules.yml).

panels.title: In-flight requests — being processed right now
panels.description: Requests currently executing; on a CPU-only host more than ~3 means queuing.

panels.title: Images captioned — successful, over the selected time range
panels.description: Successful captions in the dashboard's time range, single + bulk.

panels.title: p95 inference latency — per image, last 5 min
panels.description: 95% of images finish faster than this. Orange > 3 s, red > 8 s (CPU model).

panels.title: Error ratio — failed ÷ all images, last 5 min
panels.description: Share of images that errored (bad file, corrupt ZIP member, model failure).

panels.title: System CPU — all cores, last 1 min
panels.description: Whole-machine CPU busy percentage from node_exporter.

panels.title: 2 · Throughput and latency
Throughput — images captioned per minute, by mode [y: linear]
panels.description:
How fast the app turns images into captions. Bulk jobs show as plateaus; single uploads as small blips.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Images per minute, linear scale.

panels.title: Inference latency percentiles — p50 / p95 / p99 per image [y: linear]
panels.description:
Spread of per-image model time. A widening gap between p50 and p99 means some images are much slower, typically under CPU contention.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Seconds per image, linear scale.

panels.title: Mean inference time — from Summary _sum ÷ _count, by mode [y: linear]
panels.description:
Average model time per image, derived from the Summary's _sum and _count series (rate of sum over rate of count).
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Seconds per image, linear scale.

panels.title: Request duration p95 — end-to-end, single vs bulk [y: log10]
panels.description:
Bulk requests take orders of magnitude longer than single ones (a ZIP is one request), so a log axis keeps both readable.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Seconds per request, log10 scale.

panels.title: Requests per minute — by mode and outcome [y: linear]
panels.description:
User actions per minute (a ZIP counts once). 'partial' = ZIP with at least one failed image.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Requests per minute, linear scale.

panels.title: Inference time distribution — histogram buckets over time [y: bucket upper bound, s]
panels.description:
Each column is a moment in time; brighter cells mean more images landed in that latency bucket. Shows the full shape of latency, not just percentiles.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Seconds per image, bucket boundaries.

panels.title: 3 · Application internals
In-flight requests — active requests by mode [y: linear]
panels.description:
Concurrency inside the app. Climbing values while throughput is flat indicate a backlog.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Active requests, linear scale.

panels.title: Bulk job progress — current ZIP, 0–100%
panels.description: Completion of the bulk ZIP being processed right now; 0 when idle.

panels.title: Bulk images remaining — queue depth of running ZIP [y: linear]
panels.description:
Images left in the active ZIP; falls linearly if inference time is steady.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Images remaining, linear scale.

panels.title: Errors — per minute, by mode and type [y: linear]
panels.description:
Which failures happen and where: bad_image, bad_zip, inference, zip_too_large, empty_zip.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Errors per minute, linear scale.

defaults.noValue: No errors in this time range

panels.title: Upload volume — bytes received per second, by mode [y: linear]
panels.description:
Incoming image data. Large ZIPs raise memory and decode work even before inference starts.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Bytes per second, linear scale.

panels.title: Mean caption length — characters, from Summary _sum ÷ _count [y: linear]
panels.description:
Average generated caption length; sudden changes can reveal model or input drift.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Characters per caption, linear scale.

panels.title: App memory — process RSS vs model weights [y: linear]
panels.description:
Resident memory of the app process against the memory taken by model weights alone; the gap is runtime, images and buffers.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Memory (bytes), linear scale.

panels.title: 4 · System resources (node_exporter)
CPU utilisation by mode — stacked share of all cores [y: linear]
panels.description:
Where the CPU time goes. Inference should show up as 'user'; 'iowait' means disk is the bottleneck.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: CPU time (% of all cores), linear scale.

panels.title: Memory — used vs total [y: linear]
panels.description:
System RAM in use (total minus available) against installed RAM.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Memory (bytes), linear scale.

panels.title: Disk usage — root filesystem
panels.description: Percentage of the root filesystem in use.

panels.title: Disk I/O — read vs write throughput [y: linear]
panels.description:
Bytes per second hitting disk; spikes on first run reflect model-weight loading.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Bytes per second, linear scale.

panels.title: Network — receive vs transmit [y: linear]
panels.description:
Network traffic excluding loopback and container bridges.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Bytes per second, linear scale.

panels.title: Load average — 1-minute load vs core count [y: linear]
panels.description:
Runnable processes against available cores; load above the core line means work is queuing for CPU.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Load / cores, linear scale.

panels.title: 5 · Correlation: application load vs hardware
Bulk load vs system CPU — img/min (left) and CPU % (right) [y: linear]
panels.description:
Story: when a bulk ZIP starts, throughput rises and system CPU climbs with it, showing inference is CPU-bound.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Images per minute, linear scale.

panels.title: p95 latency vs system CPU — seconds (left) and CPU % (right) [y: linear]
panels.description:
Story: per-image latency rises as CPU saturates, typically when single uploads overlap a running bulk job.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Seconds per image, linear scale.

panels.title: In-flight requests vs system CPU — requests (left) and CPU % (right) [y: linear]
panels.description:
Story: concurrency drives CPU. Each extra in-flight request adds a step to CPU utilisation.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Active requests, linear scale.

panels.title: App share of CPU vs whole system — percent of all cores [y: linear]
panels.description:
Story: how much of the machine's CPU belongs to the app. Equal lines mean the app is the cause; a gap means other processes compete.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: CPU (% of all cores), linear scale.

panels.title: App memory vs system memory — bytes [y: linear]
panels.description:
Story: the app's resident memory (steps up at model load, grows during bulk) against total system RAM in use.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Memory (bytes), linear scale.

panels.title: 6 · Clients
Top clients — images processed per source IP [range total]
panels.description: Which source IPs generated the most work in the selected time range, split by success/error.

panels.title: Requests per browser session — top 8 [range total]
panels.description: Sessions (short hash of the Streamlit session id) ranked by number of requests in the selected range.

panels.title: Requests by client IP — top 5, per minute [y: linear]
panels.description:
Traffic per source IP over time; reveals a single client dominating the box.
X-axis: Time (local). Y-axis: Requests per minute, linear scale.
